answer.rationale: Competitor price cuts and rising churn conversations create pressure to respond with promotional pricing, but memory_73/exp_73 clearly show targeted discounting drives short-term acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention, undermining sustainable qualified revenue—the stated primary objective. That option is explicitly flagged as non-generalizable. Instead, doubling down on signup simplification and shortened onboarding (memory_31, memory_86/exp_86, confirmed) addresses the same SMB price-sensitive segment by improving activation, completion, and time-to-value without the retention harm seen in discounting. Activation messaging (memory_91) is complementary but less validated at scale than onboarding simplification. Referral incentives (memory_57) target established customers, not the price-pressured SMB segment in crisis, and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is irrelevant to the SMB churn issue at hand. Given verification budget is exhausted, I avoid promotional pricing given known downstream harm and choose the best-supported, risk-managed lever available. Scaling as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) preserves ability to monitor retention impact before wider commitment, since combining onboarding changes with the current competitive pressure introduces some new context not previously tested.
